title: Formalizing throughput fidelity: measurement definitions, customer notice flows, and credit arbitration protocol
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Customers on Dedicated capacity ask for deterministic token throughput guarantees but contracts fail to define measurement windows, burst allowances, and operator arbitration processes. This ticket defines: (1) a clear measurement spec for throughput fidelity, (2) customer notice and remediation flows when commitments are missed, and (3) a structured credit arbitration protocol for disputed incidents. Goal: ship an SLA appendix and internal runbook that legal, sales, support, and on-call can reference.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement spec doc that specifies sampling frequency, percentile(s) used, and window semantics (rolling vs fixed) approved by SRE and Legal
Customer-facing SLA appendix draft with plain-language notice templates and remediation options reviewed by Sales and Legal
Internal arbitration runbook with metrics owners, evidence requirements, timeline for decisions, and credit computation examples
Automated dashboards (dev-only) that surface the SLA metric, per-customer windows, and a synthetic baseline signal for post-incident verification
decisions: Use 99th-percentile over a rolling 60-minute window as the primary throughput compliance metric (SRE-approved)
Introduce a 5-minute burst allowance bucket per customer that does not count toward SLA violations if average over subsequent 60 minutes remains within target
Compute credits as proportional token-minute reduction over the affected billing day using a capped multiplier (legal dictated cap of 25% monthly credit)
tradeoffs: Stricter percentiles (e.g., 99.9p) reduce false negatives but increase credit exposure and measurement noise; settled on 99p for balance. Rolling windows are more protective of customers but harder to explain in plain contracts—we add clear examples in the appendix.

risks: Measurement disagreements with customers (noise), complex contract language leading to long sales cycles, edge-case exclusions (regional failovers) being exploited. Mitigation: synthetic evidence, clear examples in appendix, escrow timeline for disputes.
notes: We chose rolling-window + burst allowance to align with real traffic patterns observed in top 10 Dedicated customers. The arbitration protocol requires telemetry retention for 90 days (coord with infra).
